ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, \(PA\) and \(PB\) are tangents to circle \(\odot O\) at points \(A\) and \(B\), respectively, and \(\angle P=70^\circ\). If point \(C\) is on circle \(\odot O\) and does not coincide with \(A\) or \(B\), what is the measure of \(\angle ACB\)?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw OA, OB, \\
$ \because $ PA, PB are tangents to circle $O$ at points A, B, and $ \angle P=70^\circ$, \\
$ \therefore \angle AOB=360^\circ-90^\circ-90^\circ-\angle P=110^\circ$\\
When C is on the major arc $ \overset{\frown}{ACB}$,\\
$ \angle ACB=\frac{1}{2}\angle AOB=55^\circ$\\
When point C is on the minor arc $ \overset{\frown}{AB}$, quadrilateral ACBC$_{1}$ is a circumscribed quadrilateral\\
Then $ \angle A{C}_{1}B+\angle C=180^\circ$\\
$ \therefore \angle A{C}_{1}B=125^\circ$\\
Hence, the answer is: $\boxed{55^\circ}$ or $\boxed{125^\circ}$.

Reasoning: Connect radii OA and OB. Since PA and PB are respectively the tangents to the circle at A and B, the radii are perpendicular to the tangents, that is, ∠OAP=90° and ∠OBP=90°. In quadrilateral AOBP, the sum of the interior angles is 360°, and ∠P=70°, so ∠AOB=360°−90°−90°−70°=110°. Therefore the measure of the minor arc AB is 110°, and the measure of the major arc AB is 250°. According to the inscribed angle theorem, ∠ACB equals half the measure of the arc AB it subtends that does not contain C. If C is on the major arc AB, then ∠ACB=110°/2=55°; if C is on the minor arc AB, then ∠ACB=250°/2=125°.

From the text, the angle between the two tangents is 70°.
